title: AI generates every page of my coloring app, which began as a website and ended up as a Play Store game
author: Icy-Class-3793
selftext:
Colors Goods started as a simple coloring website. I wanted to use AI to create the line art, because drawing hundreds of coloring pages by hand was never going to happen.

The AI does two jobs. One is the library itself. All the illustrations are generated with AI, and then I go through the results, keep the ones that look clean and cute, and throw away the rest. There is a lot of weird output before you land on something actually colorable. The other job is a tool that takes any photo and turns it into line art in seconds, all inside the browser. The image never leaves the device, which felt like the right way to do it.

The site found its audience, so I wrapped it into an Android app. It is now live on the Play Store, listed as a casual game, with 1K+ downloads already:  


[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.colorsgoods.bionlabs.app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.colorsgoods.bionlabs.app)

https://preview.redd.it/94g53bgsjjjh1.png?width=503&format=png&auto=webp&s=ea834c9b0755cedc2c17e00d8f576003add16adc

The[ browser version (site)](https://colorsgoods.com) is still up and gets updated alongside the app:

It is free, localized in 6 languages, and you do not need an account to use it. The stack is React + Vite + Cloudflare, and the app runs the same codebase wrapped for Android.

If anyone here has thoughts on making the photo to line art conversion cleaner, or on running client side models in the browser, I would love to hear them. Still learning a lot of this as I go.
